title: UAE Trade License Guide: Types, Cost & How to Get One
summary: Learn what a UAE trade licence is, the different licence types, costs, required documents, how to apply, and which licence best suits your business.
body_markdown:
## What is a UAE trade license?


A trade licence is the official authorisation you need to operate a business in the UAE. If you set up your business on the mainland, the licence is issued by the relevant[Department of Economy or Economic Development](https://www.investindubai.gov.ae/en/business-setup/business-setup-services/request-to-issue-a-trade-licence) . If your business is in one of the free zones, then it is issued by the authority governing that particular free zone.


The licence also defines what your business is legally allowed to do. While a company can include multiple approved business activities under one licence, those activities must fall within the permitted scope of the licence type you choose.


### Is there a difference between a business licence and a trade licence in the UAE?


Practically speaking, there is no difference between a business and a trade licence in the UAE. The term "trade licence" is the official term used to refer to the document issued by the licensing authority, while "business licence" is the more casual, internationally familiar term that people commonly use to describe the same approval.


## Why is having a trade licence important in the UAE?


Besides the obvious factor, i.e its a mandatory legal requirement to have, a valid and the right trade licence is a must because it allows you to:


- Issue invoices and sign commercial contracts.
- Open a corporate bank account.
- Sponsor employee and investor visas where applicable.
- Register for VAT or corporate tax when required.
- Bid for Government tenders or client contracts.


## The types of UAE trade licences you can apply for


There are seven types of UAE business licences you can apply for. Each one is designed for a specific purpose and has specific requirements or constraints on what you can do with it.


Type of Licence Who is it for? Additional information


Commercial Retailers, wholesalers, trading companies, logistics businesses, eCommerce companies. The most commonly issued licence, especially on the mainland. It covers buying, selling, importing, exporting, and distributing goods.


Professional Businesses providing services based on specialised knowledge, skills, or expertise. Typically no minimum capital requirement. Allows the holder to work with any client or employer in the UAE.


Industrial Manufacturing, assembly, and industrial production businesses. Requires a physical facility suited to the activity. Certain sectors, such as oil and gas extraction and refining, are restricted to UAE national ownership.


Tourism Travel and hospitality businesses. Requires approval from the Department of Tourism and Commerce Marketing in addition to the standard licensing authority.


Freelance Individuals operating independently without a larger corporate structure. Commonly used in media, tech, and consulting-focused free zones.


Agriculture Farming, crop production, livestock, fisheries, and related activities. A niche category with land-use and environmental compliance requirements attached.


Crafts Skilled manual trades such as carpentry, metalwork, electrical maintenance, plumbing, and traditional artisan work. Used mostly by individual tradespeople rather than corporate entities.


## Mainland vs free zone trade licence: which one is right for you?


Across Alaan customers, 87% hold a mainland license and 13% hold a freezone license. A mainland licence is generally better suited to businesses that want to serve customers throughout the UAE, bid for government projects or establish a physical presence across multiple emirate.


Businesses prefered freezone license because they allow 100% foreign ownership but e 2021 amendments the Commercial Companies Law alloed foreign ownership for most mainland activities, thus taking away the biggest selling point of freezone licenses.


A free zone licence, on the other hand, is better suited for startups, international businesses and entrepreneurs looking for[faster incorporation, with simplified administration](https://www.moet.gov.ae/en/establishing-business-in-free-zones) , serving clients outside UAE, or need a virtual or flexible office.

## Jurisdiction options: which emirate suits your business?


What each license offers and requires doesn't change much between emirates. That said, you can enjoy varying levels of advantages with the same license across different emirates.


### Dubai


Dubai is often the preferred choice for businesses that intend to target international markets, financial services, technology companies, and firms. You also gain credibility with a globally recognised business address.


### Abu Dhabi


Abu Dhabi offers a better support ecosystem for businesses operating in energy, manufacturing, healthcare and government-related sectors.


### Sharjah


Sharjah is best known for the advantages it offers for manufacturing, publishing, education and creative industries. The biggest plus, however, is that those advantages come with competitive operating costs.


### Ras Al Khaimah


Ras Al Khaimah is preferred by SMEs and international entrepreneurs for the competitive setup costs and flexible licensing options the emirate offers.


### Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain


These emirates offer lower operating costs for businesses that are looking for a cost-efficient way to establish themselves in the UAE without needing the advantages of Dubai's strategic location.


## How much does a UAE trade licence cost?


There isn't a single price for a UAE trade licence because several factors influence the final cost of a licence, such as your chosen emirate or free zone, the business activity, the specific type of licence and so on. According to Alaan customer spend data, the median commercial license payment was AED 11,920 against AED 2,908 for service licenses, roughly 4 times cheaper than commercial license.


That said, generally:


- Mainland commercial licenses in Dubai typically range from AED 12,500–38,000 or more, depending on activity and approvals required.
- Professional licenses often start lower, since they don't usually require a mandated office space tied to manufacturing or trading activity.
- Free zone licenses tend to sit at the lower end overall, somewhere in the ballpark of AED 4,900–13,000+, especially in the Northern Emirates.


## The documents required to apply for a UAE trade licence


The most common documents you will need to apply for a UAE trade licence are:


- Passport copies of all shareholders and managers.
- [Emirates ID](https://u.ae/en/information-and-services/visa-and-emirates-id/emirates-id) and visa copy (where applicable).
- Reserved trade name certificate.
- Initial approval certificate, if required.
- [Memorandum of Association (MOA)](https://www.alaan.com/blog/what-is-moa-in-uae) or Articles of Association (AOA), depending on the company structure.
- Tenancy contract or Ejari certificate, if your licence requires you to set up an office.
- Business plan for certain regulated or specialised activities.


You may require additional documentation, such as external approvals for activities such as healthcare, education, financial services, or tourism, or based on the specific free zone or mainland authority you are setting up your business in.


## The steps involved in getting a UAE trade licence


Generally, the steps involved in getting a UAE trade licence are as listed below. That said, expect slight variations in the process when applying for a mainland licence vs one in any of the free zones.


- **Choose your business activity:** The business activity, as detailed earlier, determines your license type and, often, the jurisdiction options you are limited to.
- **Choose your jurisdiction:** Based on your available options, pick between a mainland or free zone in a specific emirate.
- **Reserve your trade name:** Check your shortlisted names against the available list and ensure they follow the prescribed naming conventions.
- **Get initial approval:** Confirm that the government has no objection to you starting the business.
- **Submit your MOA and tenancy documents:** An application for a mainland company will need both. In the case of a free zone, the requirements vary based on the governing authority.
- **Pay the license fees:** Once documentation clears, pay the prescribed fees.
- **Receive your license:** You're now legally authorised to operate.


Most mainland licensing authorities and free zones now allow businesses to complete much of the application process online. For the former, via the relevant Department of Economy portal in their emirate, and for the latter, directly through individual free zone websites.


## Renewing your trade license


It's essential to note that your trade license needs to be renewed annually. The process is generally simpler than the initial application as long as there are no changes to your business's information. Many licensing authorities also allow businesses to begin the renewal process before the licence expires to eliminate last-minute hiccups.


## Summing it up


The licence type you choose decides everything from what you're legally allowed to do, where your business can operate, and the initial startup capital expenditure. Get this right, and the rest of the process progresses easily. It also eliminates the need to make amendments later on down the line.

## FAQs


**Can one trade license cover multiple business activities?**


In some cases, mainland commercial licenses can cover up to 10 activities under DET's grouped activity system. Several free zones now also allow combining commercial and professional activities under one license. That said, always confirm with your specific authority if you are in doubt.


**What happens if my trade license expires before renewal?**


If you continue to operate on an expired trade licence, you will automatically attract penalties. Your banking transactions, visa approvals and other administrative processes will also be put on hold till the licence is renewed.


**Do I need a trade license to freelance in the UAE?**


Yes, you do need a freelance licence to operate as a freelancer in the UAE.
